timeline.event: The mound-building Marajoara culture emerges at the mouth of the Amazon
timeline.label: c. 400 CE

timeline.event: Pedro Álvares Cabral's fleet reaches Brazil
Salvador is founded as the colonial capital
Rio de Janeiro is founded by Estácio de Sá
The Dutch capture Olinda and Recife in Pernambuco
The colonial capital moves from Salvador to Rio de Janeiro
The Portuguese royal court arrives, fleeing Napoleon's invasion
Dom Pedro declares independence on the banks of the Ipiranga
The War of the Triple Alliance against Paraguay begins
The Golden Law abolishes slavery
Emperor Pedro II is deposed and a republic is proclaimed
The Christ the Redeemer statue is inaugurated
Getúlio Vargas proclaims the Estado Novo
Brazil hosts the World Cup and loses the deciding match at the Maracanã
Brasília is inaugurated as the new capital
The military takes power in a coup
A new democratic constitution is promulgated
The Real Plan introduces a new currency, the real
Brazil wins a record fifth World Cup
Rio de Janeiro hosts South America's first Olympic Games

places.name: Christ the Redeemer
places.clue: The statue's outstretched arms span about 28 m from the summit of Corcovado mountain above Rio.

places.name: Brasília
places.clue: Planned by Lúcio Costa and built in just a few years, its layout is often likened to an airplane or a bird in flight.

places.name: São Paulo
places.clue: The Southern Hemisphere's biggest city is home to the largest Japanese community anywhere outside Japan.

places.name: Iguaçu Falls
places.clue: Around 275 separate cascades thunder along this horseshoe of cliffs on the border with Argentina.

places.name: Manaus
places.clue: Rubber-boom fortunes built a grand opera house here, deep in the rainforest where the Rio Negro meets the Amazon.

places.name: Salvador
places.clue: The country's first capital, its hilltop Pelourinho district is lined with pastel colonial facades.

places.name: Lençóis Maranhenses
places.clue: Each rainy season, rainwater collects between its white dunes, forming thousands of blue lagoons.

places.name: Pantanal
places.clue: The world's largest tropical wetland offers some of the best chances anywhere to spot wild jaguars.

places.name: Ouro Preto
places.clue: This baroque gold-rush town is filled with churches adorned by the sculptor Aleijadinho.

places.name: Olinda
places.clue: Its hilltop colonial churches overlook neighbouring Recife, and its Carnival parades feature giant puppets.

places.name: Chapada Diamantina
places.clue: Table mountains, caves and waterfalls rise from these highlands, once a frenzied diamond-mining frontier.

places.name: Serra da Capivara
places.clue: Its rock shelters hold thousands of prehistoric paintings, among the oldest known rock art in the Americas.
